title: The discounted dividend measure on a finite set of active payment times is bounded by the sum of the discounted verification-value drops, under the two separate generator and gradient inequalities
author: @WillR
source: The separated-hypothesis variant of the Proved theorem local_verification_capped_finset_dividendMeasure_bound, which assumes the HJB equality max (X.generator w y - q * w y) (1 - deriv w y) = 0. The two separate inequalities X.generator w y - q * w y ≤ 0 and 1 ≤ deriv w y imply only that the maximum is nonpositive, so the HJB form is not available to the target local_verification_separated_countable_dividend_budget, whose hypotheses are the separate ones. That target is the countable budget of the local verification argument, and its proof applies the finite budget to the finitely many jump times below each index of an enumeration of the countable set of active payment times and then passes to the limit, so it needs this finite budget in the separated form. This is the finite counterpart of the Proved theorem local_verification_capped_countable_dividendMeasure_bound_separated, which gives the same comparison on a countable set of times.

title: The dividend measure is carried by the countable set of right jumps when it has no continuous part on the non-negative half-line
author: @WillR
source: The non-negative-range variant of the published theorem dividendMeasure_countable_rightJump_concentration_of_purely_atomic. The measure of an interval (a, b] for the dividend measure is the increase of the right limit of the dividend path, which decomposes into the sum of the right jumps of that path in the interval plus a continuous part; the hypothesis hatomic is the assumption that the continuous part vanishes. Together with the Proved countability of the right-jump set, dividendStrategy_countable_rightJump_times, this makes the dividend measure carried by a countable set, which is what allows a countable budget for the discounted dividends to bound the dividend measure of a dividend strategy. The restriction 0 <= a is what the unbounded-variation stochastic core needs, since the right-jump set of the dividend path is contained in the non-negative half-line, and it avoids asking for the statement on intervals that reach below the origin, where the right limit of the dividend path at the origin need not vanish for a general dividend strategy.

title: The Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure of a dividend strategy without a continuous part is carried by the countable set of its right jumps
author: @WillR
source: The corrected countable right-jump concentration statement for the Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure of a dividend strategy. The measure of an interval (a, b] for the dividend measure is the increase of the right limit of the dividend path, which decomposes into the sum of the right jumps of that path in the interval plus a continuous part; the hypothesis hatomic is the assumption that the continuous part vanishes. Together with the Proved countability of the right-jump set, dividendStrategy_countable_rightJump_times, this makes the dividend measure carried by a countable set, which is what allows a countable budget for the discounted dividends to bound the dividend measure of a dividend strategy. This supersedes the earlier statement dividendMeasure_countable_rightJump_concentration, which omitted the no-continuous-part hypothesis and is therefore false for a general dividend strategy.

title: A five-dimensional space of rational functions of u containing 1, u, u⁻¹ carries a 2×3 configuration iff it is D1, D2a or D2b
author: @carlok
source: Not found in the sources read: the “only if” half, the classification. Applied to conjugation hulls (with DiazModulus.rational_conj_hull_le_adjoin) it gives the five-dimensional case of Theorem F (DiazModulus.rational_conj_hull_two_by_three_configuration_iff). Theorem F asks the question of Theorem E of the mission's research note on polynomial and Laurent hulls (DiazModulus.laurent_conj_hull_two_by_three_configuration_iff, Laurent z) for every z rational in u, and builds on Theorem B (DiazModulus.circle_point_extension_two_by_three_configuration_iff, 10.6), which holds for every complex z. For Laurent z, agreement with Theorem E's classes was checked by exact computation, not proved. Its configurations give, at a candidate, exclusions that are substitutions in Roy's strong six exponentials theorem (D. Roy, Matrices whose coefficients are linear forms in logarithms, J. Number Theory 41 (1992), 22–47, Cor. 2). Uses DiazModulus.degree_two_configuration_normal_form, DiazModulus.quadratic_two_orbit_space_carries_two_by_three_configuration, DiazModulus.quadratic_cyclic_space_carries_two_by_three_configuration, DiazModulus.rational_space_configuration_coprime_ratio, DiazModulus.mobius_ratio_configuration_u_multiplier_triple and DiazModulus.two_by_three_configuration_ratio_degree_le_two. R20 of the Diaz modulus mission. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 23 October 2026 (C. Perassi).

title: GMP member top-up ceases with member payments
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: Fixed-point complex multiplication adds input error and fewer than two ulps
author: @marwahaha
source: Numerical component of the BitDFT.fixed_point_multiplication obligation. The proof derives the scalar round-toward-zero error from floor/ceiling bounds, combines the two coordinate errors using the complex norm triangle inequality, and uses the product perturbation identity (a-u)b + u(b-v). This theorem proves only the numerical error bound; it does not construct the multitape multiplication machine required by the parent theorem.

title: No GMP top-up before the member GMP payable date
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: GMP commencing on 6 April waits for later 6 April
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: Survivor statutory guarantee overlays option-linked benefit
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: Pre-88 GMP has nil section 109 increase
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.

title: Smooth projective curve covers over a finite intermediate field, with dimension bound
author: @tomasz
source: Derived from the Proved geometric-curve cover https://prove2.me/theorems/98944e77-2d0a-41a3-bad1-20bd6211e2e8 and relative field descent https://prove2.me/theorems/8113d2fc-8253-4a8a-a56e-405a6f283432 . The projective embedding is retained using the Proved projective-space base-change theorem https://prove2.me/theorems/b0c3d8f6-bffa-515d-a45a-3c3271585c3d and faithfully flat descent of closed immersions https://prove2.me/theorems/15a640ab-f9cc-514b-bd68-f574dde1accc . The relative descent argument is the algebraic-field-extension form of Stacks Project Lemma 32.10.1, https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZM . This is a strengthened finite-field curve-cover input for the Philippon mission, not a proof of its remaining global alteration step.

title: A machine wrapper for header conversion and exact vector scaling
author: @marwahaha
source:
Original machine-interface lemma for this mission; fixed-size multiplication strategy from Harvey–van der Hoeven 2025, Lemma 3.2, https://arxiv.org/html/2503.22848v1#S3.SS4. Header conversion and output scaling are additional explicit construction obligations.

Verified input-parsing components (2026-10-24): BitDFT.header_reader_correct, https://prove2.me/theorems/c527fd43-000a-4663-afc8-f8a5c254188c (exact full run); BitDFT.header_reader_ready, https://prove2.me/theorems/cf195e45-6315-41e5-ae84-fa654fa5e1c9 (configuration-level handoff before scanning the remainder); BitDFT.requested_header_reader_bound, https://prove2.me/theorems/d38db03e-afb2-448e-bb13-2385952acfb7 (actual request encoding, at most 16*n*q transitions). These are proved components for the implementation, not a completed decomposition or proof of this rescaling theorem. Remaining construction: precision-header rewriting, composition with arbitrary A, and exact multiplier-backed output scaling/serialization.

A verified controller-composition component is now available: BitDFT.machine_sequence_bound, https://prove2.me/theorems/4883f155-228c-454f-a372-2cfe442c651e (accepted proof https://prove2.me/submissions/6788a4f1-5399-4b34-ba44-03190930f57a). Compatible finite controllers compose in at most t+1+u transitions while preserving the exact tape contents and head positions at handoff. This component requires a shared alphabet and tape layout; the wrapper still needs concrete stages, alphabet/bank adapters, header arithmetic, and output scaling. It is not a completed proof or decomposition of this theorem.

The header reader now has a verified composable stopping stage: https://prove2.me/theorems/ac6acb94-e476-407e-8af2-c6a4e48e6785 (accepted proof https://prove2.me/submissions/bf38b8bf-bec9-481c-9cfe-12bd47766034). It freezes at the internal boundary after 2k+3 steps, preserving the full parser handoff configuration without copying the remaining vector. The precision rewrite, output-scaling stages, and their complete assembly remain unproved.

Verified workspace extension: https://prove2.me/theorems/574a2a6a-9bbf-4ba3-9709-71f17e6ea2a0 (proof https://prove2.me/submissions/50906bdf-1973-4ef5-9846-6f03b2c08761). Any fixed number of extra tapes can retain arbitrary caller data while the old machine runs at exactly the same clock; ordinary binary-input halting and output are preserved. This adapter still needs to be instantiated in the concrete rescaling construction.

Verified precision-arithmetic routine: BitDFT.binary_counter_add, https://prove2.me/theorems/704c4f07-84ff-4415-9649-6f681848f0ff (accepted proof https://prove2.me/submissions/c22eb590-d8e2-4375-92e3-7e9583d2a717). The fixed four-tape machine adds a unary count K to a little-endian binary word w in at most 5K+2|w|+1 actual transitions, clears the unary tape and preserves parked native input/output data. With prepared K=3 lg(n)+5 and reversed precision bits, this implements the guard-precision arithmetic. Constructing K, reversing/serializing the header bits, and complete wrapper assembly remain separate obligations.

Verified logarithmic increment preparation: BitDFT.log_scanner_correct, https://prove2.me/theorems/9ecd9597-1ef3-488d-9b05-ef6eba2ba9ec (proof https://prove2.me/submissions/9b4969b7-ba68-4244-8faf-db6c1dba1f2e). From a canonical dimension word on its work tape, a fixed finite scanner produces K=3 lg(n)+5 unary marks in exactly K+3 transitions, preserving the dimension and parked caller data and leaving the unary head on the last mark. The scanner handles n=1 and powers of two. This supplies the count formerly assumed prepared by the binary-counter specialization; their complete composition and the rest of the wrapper still require proof.

Verified combined precision-computation program: https://prove2.me/theorems/f79da9c6-12c0-43a0-bd30-5f4d2ec309d6 (accepted proof https://prove2.me/submissions/9a1b16c0-d8a2-4192-9be8-d347c5fb74e7). One fixed five-tape machine, given a canonical dimension word and reversed requested-precision bits in its prepared work layout, constructs its own logarithmic unary count and computes q=b+3 lg(n)+5 within 7q actual transitions. Its output word has at most q bits; the exact final configuration retains the dimension and caller data and clears the unary workspace. The proof composes the scanner and bounded-output counter through the accepted tape adapters and finite sequencing theorem. Installing the initial words from the request, serializing q, calling A, and scaling outputs remain unproved parts of this wrapper.

Latest verified construction progress (2026-10-24): BitDFT.encoded_precision_correct, https://prove2.me/theorems/b6fc588b-9e05-49d4-9dca-2609ce389463 (accepted proof https://prove2.me/submissions/49870642-bcb6-459a-b486-dfdf123fd3e5); BitDFT.serialize_field_correct, https://prove2.me/theorems/a96b6719-f57d-4de0-bd32-9517ee62217d (accepted proof https://prove2.me/submissions/d1dbc663-d495-4657-ac0a-7ff20fbeb026). The native-input precision machine now starts from the actual encNat(n) encNat(b) suffix encoding and computes q within 11q transitions, with a positive little-endian output word of length at most q and a full final-configuration contract. This discharges the earlier prepared-header and prepared-count assumptions for that stage. The field serializer appends an exact self-delimiting header in 2|v|+3 transitions with caller tapes preserved. Canonicalization and assembly of the full rewritten request, arbitrary-A simulation, and multiplier-based output scaling remain obligations; this theorem is still Open, and these supporting results are not a completed decomposition of it.

author: @tomasz
source: Application to the Philippon global curve-fibration alteration frontier https://prove2.me/theorems/842dbd70-6333-40fa-86df-02394eb67249 . Combines the Proved actual finite-base covering-family theorem https://prove2.me/theorems/ae594a3b-8d61-41b8-8e72-b6a40e8b9e2f and the Proved normal projective family-completion theorem https://prove2.me/theorems/77bad564-392b-4202-9bf6-e267f19ec58c . A dense absolute smooth base open is obtained over the perfect field; an absolute projective immersion is constructed from the relative projective model; equality of the global maps over the original base extends from their exact equality on the retained dense open by reducedness and separatedness. This is a global normal model, not the final global smooth alteration.

title: Post-88 GMP increases but pre-88 GMP does not
author: @WillR
source: Original explicitly specified UK pension scheme model. Pension Schemes Act 1993 s109: full annual post-1988 GMP statutory order with cap of 3%, effective 6 April after the GMP becomes payable, without first-period pro-rating; no corresponding statutory increase to pre-1988 GMP. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1993/48/section/109. HMRC GMP first-increase guidance: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/provide-a-pension-for-your-scheme-member. Section 110 sets GMP increase funding restrictions and Pensions Act 1995 s53 provides permitted reductions for other increases; not all are modelled. Anti-franking statutory sections 87-92 are NOT fully implemented: the protected-excess floor is an externally supplied illustrative minimum, not a legal certification. GMP payable date, scheme-specific pre-GPD revaluation, survivor eligibility/amounts and calendar-date inputs must be independently verified for each scheme.
